explanation: In Singapore the thumbs-up is understood the same way as in the West: approval, agreement, or encouragement. It is used casually in daily life, service settings, and on social media without causing offense.
local_tip: Use it freely for everyday approval (food, service, agreement) - there's no need to avoid it the way you might in parts of the Middle East or West Africa.

also_check.note: The thumbs-up is an obscene insult there, comparable to the middle finger in the US.
A thrust-forward thumbs-up can read as a vulgar gesture rather than simple approval.
The thumbs-up is understood as positive and causes no offense, similar to Singapore.

sources.title: Offensive Gestures by Country - World Population Review
